analysis: The change to docs/developer/test.md is documentation only: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds prose near head line 2192 describing CI run-isolation regression tests. Those tests check the request header, exact run-qualified Linux and Mac runner labels with and without sizes, fallback for generic or other-run responses, and that two runs get incompatible label sets. The supplied base excerpts (units 7 and 8, lines 2267-3187) are unchanged surrounding text. I read them for related test-guidance content, such as prefix-cache tenant partition checks, GPU/native qualification limits and the loopback-only replay rule. Nothing there was altered, and nothing weakens a control or gives operators unsafe instructions. The new text does not touch the threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011, T-041 prefix cache, A-001..A-020) and does not change code, endpoints, key handling or authorization. It claims no live runner or VM test, so it does not overstate assurance. The CI runner-label isolation it describes is outside the provider threat model's scope. The CI scripts and workflow that implement these regressions were not supplied, so I cannot confirm they enforce the described behavior. That is a coverage limit, not a finding. No security regression or new attack surface identified.
